headline: High: ms-swift can write and exfiltrate training artifacts while LightZero is a non-runnable game-playing package, creating default data-leak and workflow-conflict risk if paired in a shared workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no filesystem, browser, MCP, or shell surfaces, so it cannot ingest ms-swift output by default. ms-swift can read/write files and use stdin/stdout, so a manual copy-paste or shared-file bridge could carry malicious instructions, but the pathway is not default and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies ms-swift output into a LightZero prompt or config file
IF both agents are connected through a shared text file or terminal buffer
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate terminals and avoid copy-paste between them.
Use read-only exports for any ms-swift outputs shared with LightZero.
Strip instructions from any text passed from ms-swift to LightZero.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero touches no data classes and has no file or network surfaces, but ms-swift handles datasets, checkpoints, logs, and secrets and can read/write files plus call external APIs. In a shared workspace, ms-swift can expose those artifacts even though LightZero itself is inert, so the pair creates a default workspace leakage path if co-located.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem workspace
IF ms-swift is pointed at directories containing datasets, checkpoints, logs, or hub tokens
mitigations: Place ms-swift in a separate workspace from LightZero.
Move secrets out of any shared directory before running ms-swift.
Mount shared folders read-only for LightZero.
Rotate any hub_token or sdk-token exposed in shared logs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem sandboxing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files or modify git state, so there is no symmetric write-write conflict. ms-swift can write files, spawn subprocesses, and install packages, which can still collide with LightZero if both are launched in the same directory and ms-swift mutates shared artifacts. The conflict is one-sided but real in default shared-workspace setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same writable directory
IF ms-swift writes checkpoints, logs, or config files that LightZero also reads
mitigations: Run each agent in its own directory.
Make LightZero inputs read-only.
Avoid concurrent launches against the same artifact tree.
Use separate virtual environments for ms-swift.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared outputs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightZero is a game-playing system and ms-swift is a support/training CLI that can consume files and produce outputs, so a human or orchestrator could treat LightZero-generated artifacts as authoritative inputs for ms-swift without verification. Because no explicit verification or coordination primitive is stated, the safer assumption is that output can cascade into downstream actions or reports.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs are fed into ms-swift prompts, configs, or evaluation scripts
IF no validation step checks LightZero outputs before ms-swift acts on them
mitigations: Insert a manual review step before ms-swift consumes LightZero outputs.
Require schema validation on any exchanged files.
Mark LightZero outputs as untrusted in filenames or metadata.
Limit ms-swift to read-only analysis of LightZero artifacts.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and LightZero touches no regulated data classes. ms-swift does handle secrets and many artifact types, but the profiles do not show a concrete compliance conflict between the pair. The risk is therefore limited to documented gaps rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ms-swift workflows without a matching policy
IF logs or checkpoints containing secrets are retained beyond policy
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared artifacts.
Review ms-swift log retention settings.
Delete temporary checkpoints after use.
Store secrets outside training directories.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
